analysis_type: High-precision numerical certification of positive periods and conservative native Fourier prediction envelopes over explicitly defined parameter ellipsoids and continuous month intervals; no refitting or probability-region claim

region_rule.center: Each frozen native parameter vector b1 through b9 exactly as stored; no refitting or center update
region_rule.matrix: The corresponding frozen nine-by-nine local covariance matrix is used only to define an ellipsoid and is not interpreted as posterior or confidence covariance
region_rule.ellipsoid: E={theta:(theta-center)^T C^(-1)(theta-center) <= radius^2}; require symmetric positive-definite C by high-precision Cholesky
region_rule.radius_scope: Radius four is a frozen arithmetic choice, not a confidence level, probability coverage, optimized bound or calibrated uncertainty region
region_rule.support_identity: For any vector g, the maximum of g^T(theta-center) over E is radius*sqrt(g^T C g)
region_rule.independent_relaxation: Independent coefficient relaxations may be loose but must remain conservative and do not require linearizing periods

period_rule.support: For each period p in {b4,b7}, compute p_min and p_max from the ellipsoid support in that coordinate
period_rule.positive_certificate: Require both outward-rounded period minima to be strictly positive; otherwise do not generate finite prediction or residual bounds
period_rule.critical_radius: When both period centers are positive, critical radius is min(b4/sqrt(C_b4b4),b7/sqrt(C_b7b7)); strict positivity requires radius < critical value and the limiting parameter is recorded
period_rule.negative_control: For every fold, verify that half the analytic critical radius is accepted and the exact critical radius is rejected
period_rule.zero_guard: Period minima within a scale-dependent numerical zero zone are rejected rather than mislabeled as strictly positive
period_rule.scope: Positive periods only ensure a defined Fourier model over the selected region; they do not establish unique or physical periods

prediction_rule.term_bounds: For each harmonic coefficient c and its actual sine or cosine value t, use c_min*t and c_max*t when t>=0 and reverse them when t<0; zero gives zero contribution
prediction_rule.intercept: Bound b1 separately from its ellipsoid support
prediction_rule.prediction_envelope: Sum all term minima for f_min and all term maxima for f_max; the actual trigonometric signs are used at each month and no Taylor or fixed-period approximation is substituted
prediction_rule.residual_upper_bound: For each observed y, use max(abs(y-f_min),abs(y-f_max)) conditional on the defined ellipsoid and positive periods
prediction_rule.center_consistency: Require every frozen center prediction to lie inside its available envelope and actual residual not to exceed its upper bound; this is arithmetic consistency, not external validation or probability coverage
prediction_rule.width_audit: Report envelope widths and residual upper bounds so formally valid but wide bounds cannot be called high information or new period evidence

numerical_rule.engine: mpmath with 80 decimal digits and exact decimal conversion of stored input values
numerical_rule.outward_relative_margin: Apply a relative margin of 1e-24 before conversion to binary floats, then use nextafter in the outward direction for every certified lower and upper value
numerical_rule.certificate_class: High-precision numerical interval certificate, not exact rational algebra
numerical_rule.positive_definite_check: Fail rather than generate bounds if the covariance matrix is not symmetric positive definite
numerical_rule.failure_preservation: Non-finite values, failed Cholesky, non-positive periods, exact critical radii and unavailable envelopes are retained explicitly

output_rule.word: papers/前沿共生ENSO原生椭球连续界_图文完整版.docx

prohibitions: No refitting, changed centers, changed covariance matrices, changed folds, period bounds or post-hoc radius selection
No Taylor or fixed-period substitution for the native Fourier model
No finite prediction or residual bound when either period cannot be certified positive
No probability, confidence, posterior, calibrated-coverage, optimal-radius, new-period or physical-endogeneity claim
No use of center-prediction containment or actual-residual coverage as independent scientific validation
No exact rational-certificate claim for the high-precision numerical intervals
No hiding of non-positive periods, unavailable folds, wide envelopes or numerical failures
